recipe_version.title: Saag Paneer
recipe_version.description: Browned paneer cubes simmered in a spiced spinach (saag) skillet sauce finished with cream and butter.

ingredients.name: paneer
ingredients.note: required dairy. Block paneer, not pre-crumbled. Milk allergen.
ingredients.preparation: cut into 3/4-inch cubes and patted dry

ingredients.name: baby spinach
ingredients.note: fresh. The saag greens. Frozen spinach (10 oz thawed and squeezed dry) may substitute in shopping but fresh is the written path.

ingredients.name: jalapeño
ingredients.note: seeded for medium heat; keep some seeds for hotter

ingredients.name: canned diced tomatoes
ingredients.note: one 14.5 oz can, drained of excess watery liquid but keep the tomato flesh

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.note: required dairy. Finish only. Do not skip for a HH001 claim — this meal is not HH001.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: required dairy. Mounted into the saag at the end with the cream.

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tbsp to brown the paneer, 1 tbsp for the onion base

ingredients.name: garam masala
ingredients.note: divided: 1/2 tsp with the tomato base, 1/2 tsp at the end

ingredients.name: cayenne pepper
ingredients.note: optional heat beyond the jalapeño; omit for milder

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/4 tsp on browning paneer, 1 tsp in the saag

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: to loosen the spinach puree as it simmers; add only as needed up to 1/2 cup

steps.title: Prep spinach and paneer
steps.body: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the baby spinach and cook just until collapsed, about 1 minute. Drain and rinse under cold water. Squeeze out excess water firmly. Chop the spinach roughly, or pulse a few times in a food processor to a coarse puree (not a baby-food slick). Cut the paneer into 3/4-inch cubes and pat dry. Dice the onion. Mince the garlic, ginger, and jalapeño. Measure the spices, cream, butter, oil, tomatoes, salt, cilantro, and lemon juice.

steps.title: Brown the paneer
steps.body: Heat 2 tbsp of the neutral oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the paneer cubes and 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook, turning, until golden on several sides, about 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer the paneer to a plate. Do not add meat. Do not substitute tofu in this package and still call it saag paneer.

steps.title: Build the onion-spice base
steps.body: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tbsp neutral oil. Add the yellow onion and cook until soft and lightly golden, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and jalapeño. Cook 1 minute. Stir in the ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, 1/2 tsp of the garam masala, and the optional cayenne. Stir 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer tomatoes and spinach
steps.body: Add the canned diced tomatoes and 1 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook, stirring, until the tomatoes look jammy and most free liquid has cooked down, about 5 minutes. Stir in the chopped spinach and up to 1/2 cup water as needed so the saag is saucy but not watery. Simmer about 5 minutes. This spinach-tomato saag is made in the skillet, not a jarred spinach sauce.

steps.title: Return paneer and finish with dairy
steps.body: Return the browned paneer to the skillet. Simmer 3 minutes so the cubes heat through. Stir in the heavy cream, unsalted butter, and the remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala. Warm through 1 minute without a hard boil. Take off the heat. Stir in the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve as a skillet saag with paneer cubes visible. No chicken. No lamb. kitchen_tested is false.

recipe_version.heat: Boil for spinach blanch (inside prep). Skillet medium-high for paneer, then medium for the saag base and simmer. Finish cream on low/off-hard-boil.
recipe_version.doneness: Paneer golden on several faces, soft inside, not rubbery-dry. Saag thick enough to coat a spoon, spinach cooked and green-olive rather than raw. Cream stirred smooth. kitchen_tested is false.

Compared with Moroccan Chickpea Skillet: chickpea cluster closed; this has no chickpeas. Compared with Potato-Leek Gratin / Lemon Pea Risotto: other dairy mains, different formats (bake / risotto vs spinach skillet). Compared with Black Bean Quesadillas / Harissa Carrots with Feta: dairy elsewhere, not saag. Deliberately not butter chicken (poultry + dairy would waste the Indian slot on chicken while pho/souvlaki already add poultry).
